Methods for Multivariate Ridge Regression Objects

Source: R/mlmridge.R
mlmridge-methods.Rd

Experimental. Multivariate ridge regression (class "mlmridge") is new in this version; its functions, arguments and results may change in future releases.

Basic methods for objects of class "mlmridge", returned by ridge() when the response is a matrix.

  • coef() extracts the coefficients: by default a list with one \(p \times q\) matrix for each ridge constant; with type = "array", a 3-d array indexed by [lambda, predictor, response]; with response, the \(\lambda \times p\) matrix for one response, as for a "ridge" object.

  • vcov() extracts the covariance matrices of the coefficients: by default a list with, for each ridge constant, the \(pq \times pq\) covariance matrix of the stacked coefficients \(\mathrm{vec}(\mathbf{B})\), which is kronecker(Sigma, cov[[i]]); with response, the list of \(p \times p\) matrices for one response.

  • print() shows the coefficients for each response and the optimal ridge constants given by the HKB, LW and GCV criteria, for each response and pooled over responses.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mlmridge'
coef(object, response = NULL, type = c("list", "array"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'mlmridge'
vcov(object, response = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mlmridge'
print(x, digits = max(5, getOption("digits") - 5), ...)

Arguments

object, x

An object of class "mlmridge"

response

If not NULL, a response (name or number) for which to return the results, in the same form as for a univariate "ridge" object; see as.ridge().

type

For coef() with response = NULL: "list" (the default) or "array".

...

Other arguments, not used.

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

Value

coef() and vcov() return a list, array or matrix, as described above; print() returns x, invisibly.

See also

ridge(), as.ridge()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("heplots", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data(schooldata, package = "heplots")
  sridge <- ridge(cbind(reading, mathematics, selfesteem) ~
                  education + occupation + visit + counseling + teacher,
                  data = schooldata, lambda = c(0, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 5))
  sridge
  coef(sridge)[[4]]                       # coefficients for lambda = 1
  coef(sridge, response = "reading")      # lambda x p, for one response
  dim(coef(sridge, type = "array"))
  dim(vcov(sridge)[[1]])                  # pq x pq
}
#> [1] 15 15
